caps.reason: High-impact daemon Computer Use proof and kill-switch/entitlement claims are not fully implementation-backed on the production daemon path.
Some controls lack production-mode regression tests or deployment-state verification.

findings.title: Daemon local-auth proof verifier is not wired in the production executable
Daemon browser Computer Use uses synthetic entitlement and kill-switch context
Stripe redirect URL validation accepts unsafe non-HTTPS localhost-substring hosts
Firestore App Check enforcement is deployment-state dependent and not repo-verifiable
Public HTTP endpoints lack explicit product-layer rate limiting evidence
Data deletion audit logging is best-effort
Production deploy still supports long-lived secret fallback paths
SQLCipher key creation can continue after Keychain persistence failure
Signal and E2EE privacy claims require narrower wording

threats.title: Unauthorized daemon Computer Use action after first-party process compromise
Daemon Computer Use ignores remote kill switch or entitlement suspension
Billing redirect phishing through weak return URL validation
Direct Firestore access without deployed App Check enforcement
Public endpoint denial-of-wallet or availability abuse
Irreversible deletion without durable audit evidence
Unsupported privacy or E2EE claim creates user and audit risk
Local encrypted database availability loss from non-persisted key
Remote MCP token replay or over-scoped access
Sensitive data leakage through logs or crash reports

claims.claim: Most protected callable APIs require Firebase Auth and App Check.
Firestore access is owner scoped and App Check enforced.
Hosted MCP uses scoped short-lived tokens and local decryption for sealed bodies.
All sensitive user data has Signal-quality E2EE.
Local encrypted data keys are stored in Keychain.
Daemon Computer Use requires independent local-auth proof.
Daemon Computer Use is always kill-switch and entitlement gated.
Stripe webhooks are signature verified and idempotent.
High-risk data export is fail-closed audited.
